police are often called to mental health crises, but that the Mental Health Act does not provide a legal and ethical basis to justify this.
police are often involved in the involuntary transport of people living in rural and remote areas who are experiencing a mental health emergency.
Police involvement in mental health crisis is intensified in rural areas and particularly after hours, when access to health services is further stretched.

the role of police in the involuntary care and transport of people with mental illness.
the legal and ethical basis of involuntary transport of people living in the Australian community with mental illness.
the role of police in mental health transport, the legal and ethical basis of involuntary treatment, and the implications for police involvement in mental health care in rural and remote areas.
